artifacts.summary: Empirical audit of all 19 extensions' index-entries.json against the 3 contradictory schema authorities, with a concrete migration map, meta-catch-all breakdown, Tier-1/double-load findings, and a new check-extension-docs.sh Rule T design.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system repo, index.schema.json's load_when has additionalProperties:false allowing only agents/commands/languages/always -- yet task_types is the dominant real-world key (used by 6/19 extensions, 168/470 entries incl. core's meta catch-all) and is technically forbidden by the schema. The schema was never mechanically enforced (no ajv/jsonschema validator call exists anywhere; validate-context-index.sh only cites it in a comment), which is how it drifted this far without any gate failing.

load_when.languages and load_when.skills in this repo's context index are read by NOTHING at runtime except a defensive dead-entry-check exclusion inside validate-context-budgets.sh (2 occurrences total, confirmed by exhaustive grep). The real, live-queried load_when keys are agents/commands/task_types/always (confirmed via context-discovery.md, validate-index.sh, validate-wiring.sh, lint-contract-compliance.sh). Any future audit of this index should treat languages/skills as dead weight, not a data source.

The live index-entries.json -> index.json merge engine is lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/merge.lua's M.append_index_entries -- it passes each source entry through verbatim with zero field remapping. A separate, apparently-stale merge implementation also exists inside install-extension.sh (lines ~180-260) assuming an obsolete flat-array/description-tags schema shape that no longer matches any real extension file; it is not exercised by the live deploy path but is a latent risk (silently drops commands/always from load_when in its object-shape branch) worth a future cleanup task.
